evidence: Defining behaviour is graded directly and heavily: wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live (ethical walls across list/search/post/reply/transcript/mentions/links with replay refusals plus positive controls), deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes and hold_scope_and_release (retention boundary, permanent deletion, hold overrides timer, partner-only) at weight 2.0 per part (functional judge.toml lines 144-251). Durability: the final 'persistence' criterion (weight 4.0, judge.toml lines 356-370) sets up posts, a reply, an edit with version, a hold, a deletion, a timer change and a wall, records positive controls BEFORE restart (step c, so a dead app cannot pass by doing nothing), then calls restart_app, which really kills the node process group and relaunches it on the same DB_PATH (test.sh lines 127-193; restart_mcp.py single-use marker), then requires a fresh page and re-sign-in with every item reading exactly as before. prompt.md lines 65-72 state that reload or re-sign-in in the same process is not a restart. Server-backing beyond same-origin is proven by cross-account readbacks throughout (Harriet posts, Gwen/Dev/Sian read in separate contexts; signed-out replays refused), so localStorage/in-memory facades fail; network posture does not affect this. Runtime evidence: scripted golden on current source hashes (raw-evidence-index, hashes re-verified) passes persistence_before and persistence across a real restart (restart-pids old 28 -> new 57); hosted v2 judge runs show the persistence criterion graded 'yes' for Oracle and Luna with nop=0, demonstrating the judge can drive restart_app. Conforming-alternative check: any storage file, any route/payload/cookie, and state-relative notes ('note how many results', 'Dev's exact M-13 count', 'whether Probate/Insurer letter return anything') tolerate earlier mutations and alternative designs; nothing hidden is required. Broken-app check: an in-memory store loses state at restart; a localStorage store fails cross-account readbacks. Residual risk (why risk=true): (1) no full configured judge run of these exact v3 bytes exists (index scope says so), so current-bytes judge execution of the persistence criterion is unmeasured; (2) template-controlled restart helper sends only SIGTERM, waits 5s, never SIGKILLs or checks that the new pid is alive, and probe_ready accepts any answer on :3000, so an app that traps SIGTERM and keeps serving from memory would make the 'restart' a no-op and pass. This is adversarial and template-owned (test.sh identical to template), not a task-specific defect.
